name: seg1_counter
title: "Seven-segment decimal counter with UART test shell"
board: nexys_a7_100t
part: xc7a100tcsg324-1
top: top

clocks:
  - name: clk
    port: clk
    period_ns: 10
    comment: "100 MHz board oscillator, pin E3 (CLK100MHZ)"

reset:
  name: cpu_reset
  port: cpu_resetn
  polarity: active low
  sync: true
  comment: "CPU RESET button, pin C12, active low on the board; synchronised into clk and used as an active high internal reset"

parameters:
  ONE_SEC_CYCLES: 100000000
  DEBOUNCE_CYCLES: 1000000
  SCAN_CYCLES: 100000
  BAUD_DIV_CYCLES: 868
  COUNT_DIGITS: 4
  # ONE_SEC_CYCLES: one second at 100 MHz (simulation overrides it to a small value)
  # DEBOUNCE_CYCLES: 10 ms at 100 MHz
  # SCAN_CYCLES: 1 ms per digit slot at 100 MHz
  # BAUD_DIV_CYCLES: 115200 baud at 100 MHz (100000000 / 115200 = 868)

ports:
  - name: clk
    direction: input
    width: 1
    role: "100 MHz clock, pin E3"
  - name: cpu_resetn
    direction: input
    width: 1
    role: "CPU RESET button, pin C12, active low"
  - name: btnc
    direction: input
    width: 1
    role: "centre push button, pin N17, active high, clears the count"
  - name: seg
    direction: output
    width: 8
    role: "seven-segment cathodes CA CB CC CD CE CF CG DP, pins T10 R10 K16 K13 P15 T11 L18 H15, active low"
  - name: an
    direction: output
    width: 8
    role: "digit anodes AN0 to AN7, pins J17 J18 T9 J14 P14 T14 K2 U13, active low"
  - name: uart_rxd
    direction: input
    width: 1
    role: "USB-UART receive from host into FPGA, pin C4"
  - name: uart_txd
    direction: output
    width: 1
    role: "USB-UART transmit from FPGA to host, pin D4"

behaviour:
  counter:
    - "a one-cycle tick pulse is produced every ONE_SEC_CYCLES clk cycles"
    - "the count is held in COUNT_DIGITS decimal digits with range 0000 to 9999"
    - "the count increments by one on each tick"
    - "the count wraps from 9999 to 0000 on the next tick"
    - "reset sets the count and the tick counter to 0"
  clear_button:
    - "btnc is synchronised and debounced: a press registers only after btnc stays high for DEBOUNCE_CYCLES consecutive clk cycles"
    - "a registered btnc press sets the count to 0 and restarts the tick counter from 0"
    - "btnc does not change the tick period"
  display:
    - "the binary count is converted to four BCD digits: thousands, hundreds, tens and units"
    - "digits are multiplexed: each anode is enabled for one slot of SCAN_CYCLES clk cycles and the four digit slots rotate"
    - "anodes AN4 to AN7 are held inactive (high)"
    - "leading zeros are displayed, so the count 42 shows 0042"
    - "seg is active low: a segment bit of 0 lights that segment"
    - "decimal point is held off"
  uart_shell:
    - "serial format is 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit at BAUD_DIV_CYCLES clk cycles per bit"
    - "a read of a register returns the value in the register map for that offset"
    - "the design ID register returns the ASCII bytes of SEG1"
    - "the framing of read requests is defined by the open question on the shell protocol"

registers:
  map:
    - offset: "0x00"
      name: ID
      access: RO
      reset: "0x53454731"
      bits: "31:0 ASCII bytes of SEG1, byte 3 is S, byte 0 is 1"
    - offset: "0x04"
      name: COUNT
      access: RO
      reset: "0x00000000"
      bits: "15:0 binary value of the count, range 0 to 9999"

timing:
  latency:
    tick_to_display: "count update is visible on seg within 2 SCAN_CYCLES after the tick"
    clear_to_count: "count is 0 within DEBOUNCE_CYCLES plus 2 clk cycles after btnc goes high"
    reset_to_count: "count is 0 within 2 clk cycles after cpu_resetn goes low"
  constraints:
    clock: "clk at 10 ns period, timing must close with no negative slack"
    io: "all outputs registered before the pins"

resources_expected:
  lut: 200
  ff: 150
  bram: 0
  dsp: 0
  comment: "rough estimate: 32-bit tick counter, 4 BCD digit counters, scan counter, debouncer, UART transmitter and receiver, register read mux"

interfaces_note: "no AXI4-Lite block; the UART test shell is the only register access path"

assumptions:
  - text: "pin assignments come from the Digilent Nexys A7-100T master constraints file"
    reason: "the pins listed in ports are the board pins for that file; the flow will fail on any mismatch"
  - text: "the seven-segment display is common anode and active low, and the anodes are active low"
    reason: "this is how the Nexys A7 seven-segment display is wired"
  - text: "btnc and the USB-UART lines are asynchronous and are synchronised before use"
    reason: "they come from outside the clk domain and would otherwise violate timing or cause metastability"
  - text: "one count step per second is exact to the 100 MHz oscillator with no correction"
    reason: "the oscillator is the only clock source and no tolerance is specified in the request"
  - text: "the count is binary inside the design and converted to BCD for display only"
    reason: "a binary counter is the smallest structure and BCD conversion is needed only for the four displayed digits"
  - text: "the UART shell is read-only and cannot write or clear registers"
    reason: "the request asks only for reading the count over the shell"

open_questions:
  - question: "What is the register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register) for the UART test shell?"
    default: "0x00 ID, 32 bit, RO, reset 0x53454731 (ASCII SEG1); 0x04 COUNT, 32 bit field with bits 15:0 used, RO, reset 0x00000000 (binary count)"
    reason: "the request names shell register reads and the design ID but gives no offsets, so the proposed two-register map is used until answered"
  - question: "How many digits does the counter display and what is the maximum count?"
    default: "4 digits, range 0000 to 9999, wrap to 0000"
    reason: "the request says decimal display but does not give a width; four digits fits the count range and leaves the other four anodes off"
  - question: "Are leading zeros displayed or blanked?"
    default: "leading zeros are displayed, so 42 shows 0042"
    reason: "a fixed four-digit counter reads most clearly with zeros, and blanking would need an extra rule"
  - question: "What are the UART baud rate, data bits, parity and stop bits?"
    default: "115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, BAUD_DIV_CYCLES 868"
    reason: "115200 8N1 is the usual default for the Nexys USB-UART bridge and the request gives no rate"
  - question: "What is the framing of a shell read request and response?"
    default: "one request byte 'r' followed by one offset byte, response is four bytes most significant first"
    reason: "the request does not define the protocol and a simple fixed frame is the smallest one that reads a 32 bit register"
  - question: "Does the centre button clear only the count, or also restart the one-second phase?"
    default: "clear sets the count to 0 and restarts the tick counter so the next increment is one full second later"
    reason: "restarting the phase makes the first second after a clear exactly one second long"
  - question: "What debounce time is used for btnc?"
    default: "DEBOUNCE_CYCLES 1000000 (10 ms at 100 MHz)"
    reason: "10 ms is a common mechanical bounce window and the request gives no value"
  - question: "Can the count be cleared from the UART shell as well as by btnc?"
    default: "no, the shell is read only"
    reason: "the request asks only for reading the count over the shell"
  - question: "Is the count stable during a multi-byte read or can it change between bytes?"
    default: "no snapshot: the 16 bit count may change between bytes of a read, with the value read from the live register"
    reason: "a snapshot register would add state the request does not ask for; a one-second update rate makes a mid-read change rare"
  - question: "What is the digit scan rate?"
    default: "SCAN_CYCLES 100000 (1 ms per digit slot, about 125 Hz full frame)"
    reason: "1 ms per slot avoids visible flicker with four digits and the request gives no value"

requirements:
  - id: REQ-01
    text: "After cpu_resetn goes low the count is 0000 within 2 clk cycles"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-02
    text: "The count increases by exactly one on each one-second tick"
    proof: [simulation]
  - id: REQ-03
    text: "The count wraps from 9999 to 0000 on the next tick"
    proof: [simulation, formal]
  - id: REQ-04
    text: "The tick period is ONE_SEC_CYCLES clk cycles"
    proof: [simulation]
  - id: REQ-05
    text: "A btnc press held for DEBOUNCE_CYCLES clk cycles sets the count to 0"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-06
    text: "A btnc pulse shorter than DEBOUNCE_CYCLES clk cycles does not change the count"
    proof: [simulation]
  - id: REQ-07
    text: "cpu_resetn low resets the count and the tick counter to 0"
    proof: [simulation, formal]
  - id: REQ-08
    text: "Each of the four enabled digits shows its BCD digit of the count with leading zeros"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-09
    text: "seg and an are active low, with AN4 to AN7 held high"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-10
    text: "A UART read of the ID register returns 0x53454731"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-11
    text: "A UART read of the COUNT register returns the current binary count"
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
  - id: REQ-12
    text: "Timing closes at 10 ns clk period with no negative setup slack"
    proof: [analysis]
  - id: REQ-13
    text: "The design uses no BRAM and no DSP blocks"
    proof: [analysis]

Every design embeds the test shell (`shell/rtl/fpga_shell.sv`) so that a host can test it over the board's
USB-UART without a debugger. This file is the shell's specification: the RTL, the Python model
(`shell/model/shell_model.py`) and the host driver (`shell/host/fpga_shell.py`) are all checked against it.

**Versions.** 1.1 added BUILD_ID at 0x05; a 1.0 shell answers BAD_ADDRESS there (and counts a request error). A host
reads SHELL_VERSION (0x01) first and reads 0x05 only on 1.1 or later.

## Line

- UART, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, LSB first, idle high.
- **115200 baud** by default: `CLKS_PER_BIT = 868` at 100 MHz (100e6 / 115200 = 868.06, an error of -0.007 %).
  The receiver samples each bit at its middle, so it tolerates a few per cent of baud mismatch; the cocotb tests
  check ±2 %.
- On the Nexys A7 the FPGA receives on `UART_TXD_IN` (pin C4) and sends on `UART_RXD_OUT` (pin D4); the names are
  from the host's point of view. RTS/CTS are not used.

## Frames

All multi-byte values are **little-endian** (D0 = bits 7:0). `CHK` is the XOR of the bytes between the sync byte
and `CHK`.

Request, always 8 bytes, read or write:

| Byte | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | `0xA5` | CMD | ADDR | D0 | D1 | D2 | D3 | CHK = CMD ^ ADDR ^ D0 ^ D1 ^ D2 ^ D3 |

CMD: `0x01` read (the data bytes are ignored; send zeros), `0x02` write.

Response, always 7 bytes:

| Byte | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | `0x5A` | STATUS | D0 | D1 | D2 | D3 | CHK = STATUS ^ D0 ^ D1 ^ D2 ^ D3 |

The data is the register's value for a read and the value written for a successful write (0 for a write to
STATUS). Errors return data 0.

| STATUS | Name | When |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | OK | |
| `0x01` | BAD_CHECKSUM | CHK does not match (checked first) |
| `0x02` | BAD_COMMAND | CMD is not 0x01 or 0x02 |
| `0x03` | BAD_ADDRESS | ADDR is 0x06-0x7F |
| `0x04` | READ_ONLY | a write to 0x00-0x02 or 0x05 |

## Framing and recovery rules

1. **Sync.** While idle the shell discards every byte until it sees `0xA5`; the next 7 bytes are the frame,
   whatever their values.
2. **Timeout.** If a frame stops for more than `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` clocks (100 000 = **1 ms** at 100 MHz, about 11
   byte times at 115200) between bytes, the shell drops it without answering and goes back to hunting. A host that
   gets no answer waits more than 1 ms and sends the request again.
3. **UART framing error.** A byte with a low stop bit is dropped and any part frame is abandoned (no answer).
4. **One request at a time.** The host waits for the response before sending the next request; bytes that arrive
   while the shell is still sending a response are discarded.
5. Every error above is counted in STATUS.

## Registers

| ADDR | Name | Access | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | DESIGN_ID | RO | four ASCII characters chosen by the design, MSB first (the T1 design is `"T1DC"` = `0x54314443`) |
| `0x01` | SHELL_VERSION | RO | `0x00010001` (major 1, minor 1) |
| `0x02` | BUILD_STAMP | RO | set at build time; the flow puts the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the design's source and constraint files here (`flow/prepare.py`; 0 in simulation) |
| `0x03` | SCRATCH | RW | any 32-bit value; reset 0; for loopback tests |
| `0x04` | STATUS | RO, write clears | `[7:0]` checksum errors, `[15:8]` request errors (bad command, bad address, read-only), `[23:16]` UART framing errors, `[31:24]` frame timeouts; each saturates at 255; any write sets all four to 0 |
| `0x05` | BUILD_ID | RO | the bitstream's USR_ACCESS word, read from the configuration logic through the `USR_ACCESSE2` primitive (since 1.1). The flow writes the build ID there (`flow/manifest.py`, `BITSTREAM.CONFIG.USR_ACCESS`), so this register reports the bitstream actually loaded; `SIM_BUILD_ID` in simulation |
| `0x06`-`0x7F` | reserved | | BAD_ADDRESS |
| `0x80`-`0xFF` | window | design | the design under test's registers; never an error from the shell |

## The window interface (shell to design)

| Signal | Dir | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `win_addr[6:0]` | out | ADDR - 0x80 |
| `win_wr` | out | one-cycle pulse: write `win_wdata` to `win_addr` |
| `win_rd` | out | one-cycle pulse: read `win_addr` |
| `win_wdata[31:0]` | out | |
| `win_rdata[31:0]` | in | must be valid in the cycle after `win_rd` (register it) |

`win_addr` and `win_wdata` are stable during the pulse.

## Worked bytes (the tests check these)

| What | Request | Response |
|---|---|---|
| read DESIGN_ID of the T1 design | `A5 01 00 00 00 00 00 01` | `5A 00 43 44 31 54 62` |
| write SCRATCH = `0x12345678` | `A5 02 03 78 56 34 12 09` | `5A 00 78 56 34 12 08` |
| any request with a bad CHK | | `5A 01 00 00 00 00 01` |
| write DESIGN_ID | `A5 02 00 00 00 00 00 02` | `5A 04 00 00 00 00 04` |

A full request and its response take 15 bytes x 10 bits / 115200 = **1.30 ms** on the line, plus the host's
USB latency.

# seg1_counter: architecture (stage 1, board and device planning)

Board: Nexys A7-100T, part xc7a100tcsg324-1. Top module `top`. One clock domain.
The design counts up once per second, shows the count on four seven-segment digits,
clears it from the centre button and exposes it (and the design ID) through the
UART test shell `fpga_shell`.

## Block diagram

```text
                      CLK100MHZ (100 MHz)
                            |
   CPU_RESETN --> [reset_sync] --> rst (active high, sync release)
                            |
   BTNC ----------> [btn_debounce] --- clr_pulse ---+
                    (sync2 + 10 ms hold)            |
                                                    v
   UART_TXD_IN --> +---------------------------+  +--------------+
                   |  fpga_shell (test shell)  |->| seg1_counter |
   UART_RXD_OUT <--|  uart_rx, uart_tx, core   |  | tick (1 s)   |
                   +---------------------------+  | count 0..9999|
                        win_addr/wr/rd/wdata      +------+-------+
                        win_rdata (ID, COUNT)           | count[13:0] (binary)
                                                        v
                                               +-----------------+
                                               | seg_display     |--> SEG[7:0] (registered)
                                               | BCD + 4-digit   |--> AN[7:0]  (registered)
                                               | scan, 1 ms slot |
                                               +-----------------+
```

Blocks (module, file):

| Name | Function |
|---|---|
| top (rtl/top.sv) | board top: resets, instantiates every block below and fpga_shell, ties AN4..AN7 high |
| reset_sync (shell) | synchronises CPU_RESETN into CLK100MHZ, active-high reset (async assert, sync release) |
| btn_debounce (rtl/btn_debounce.sv) | sync2 on BTNC, counts consecutive high cycles, one-cycle clr pulse after DEBOUNCE_CYCLES |
| seg1_counter (rtl/seg1_counter.sv) | 27-bit tick counter (ONE_SEC_CYCLES), 14-bit binary count 0..9999, clear on clr_pulse, window register map (ID at 0x00, COUNT at 0x04 as window offsets 0x80 / 0x84 are the shell's; see register map) |
| seg_display (rtl/seg_display.sv) | binary to four BCD digits (double dabble), digit scan counter (SCAN_CYCLES), segment decode, registered SEG and AN outputs |
| fpga_shell (shell) | UART 115200 8N1 line, frame protocol, register window |

## Register map (through the shell window)

The shell owns 0x00 to 0x7F. The design's registers sit in the window at 0x80 and up.
The spec's offsets are the design's offsets, so the window addresses are the shell address minus 0x80.

| Shell ADDR | Window win_addr | Name | Access | Reset | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x80 | 0x00 | ID | RO | 0x53454731 | ASCII "SEG1" (byte 3 = S) |
| 0x84 | 0x04 | COUNT | RO | 0x00000000 | bits [15:0] binary count, 0..9999; bits 31:16 = 0 |

Read-only: win_wr is ignored. The count is read live (no snapshot), as the spec defaults say.

## Clock plan

| Domain | Port | Frequency | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| clk | CLK100MHZ | 100 MHz (10 ns) | the only clock; tick, debounce, scan and UART all on it; no gated or derived clocks; tick is a clock-enable |

## Reset plan

- CPU_RESETN (active low, async to the board) goes through `reset_sync` (the only asynchronous-assert element,
  a reset synchroniser). Its active-high output `rst` is the only reset inside the design.
- Reset clears: tick counter, count, debounce counter, scan slot counter, and the shell's control state (inside fpga_shell).
- Datapath registers (BCD working registers, seg/an output registers) have no reset; the output registers are
  written every cycle from the scan state, which is itself reset.

## Crossings

| From | To | Signal | Primitive | Inlined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU_RESETN (async) | clk | rst | reset_sync | top |
| BTNC (async) | clk | btnc | sync2 | btn_debounce |
| UART_TXD_IN (async) | clk | uart line | sync2 | uart_rx (inside fpga_shell) |

No signal crosses clock domains other than these; there is one clock.

## Pin list (resource names; pin numbers are set by board_constraints from the master XDC)

| Top port | Board resource | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLK100MHZ | 100 MHz oscillator | in | clk |
| CPU_RESETN | CPU RESET button | in | active low |
| BTNC | centre button | in | active high |
| SEG[7:0] | CA CB CC CD CE CF CG DP | out | active low; bit 0 = CA ... bit 7 = DP |
| AN[7:0] | AN0 .. AN7 | out | active low; AN4..AN7 held high |
| UART_TXD_IN | USB-UART receive pin (host to FPGA) | in | to fpga_shell |
| UART_RXD_OUT | USB-UART transmit pin (FPGA to host) | out | from fpga_shell |

Outputs (SEG, AN, UART_RXD_OUT) are driven from registers.

## Resource prediction

| Resource | Predicted | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| lut | [120, 450] | counters (27+20+17+14 bit), BCD double dabble, segment decode, window mux, UART and shell |
| ff | [100, 350] | counters, BCD working and output registers, shell and UART state |
| bram_tile | 0 | no memory |
| dsp | 0 | no multiply |

## Library entries considered

ip_lookup was not run: the tool is not available to this agent in this session. Nothing in the library was taken.
The counter, debouncer and seven-segment scan are short and specific to this spec; the UART and test shell are
reused from `shell/rtl` (not a library entry).

## Open questions for the owner

1. Port names. The spec's port names are lowercase (clk, cpu_resetn, btnc, seg, an, uart_rxd, uart_txd). The flow
   convention is that top-level names are the master XDC's (CLK100MHZ, BTNC, UART_RXD_OUT), and the UART pair must
   be UART_TXD_IN and UART_RXD_OUT. This design uses the convention names. The owner should confirm this
   rename, since FDA-CON-8 checks the spec's ports against the top module.
2. The shell register addresses. The spec's offsets 0x00 and 0x04 are the design's window offsets; the shell
   exposes them at 0x80 and 0x84. The owner should confirm this mapping.

# seg1_counter: architecture (stage 1, board and device planning)

Board: Nexys A7-100T, part xc7a100tcsg324-1. Top module `top`. One clock domain.
The design counts up once per second, shows the count on four seven-segment digits,
clears it from the centre button and exposes it (and the design ID) through the
UART test shell `fpga_shell`.

## Block diagram

```text
                      CLK100MHZ (100 MHz)
                            |
   CPU_RESETN --> [reset_sync] --> rst (active high, sync release)
                            |
   BTNC ----------> [btn_debounce] --- clr_pulse ---+
                    (sync2 + 10 ms hold)            |
                                                    v
   UART_TXD_IN --> +---------------------------+  +--------------+
                   |  fpga_shell (test shell)  |->| seg1_counter |
   UART_RXD_OUT <--|  uart_rx, uart_tx, core   |  | tick (1 s)   |
                   +---------------------------+  | count 0..9999|
                        win_addr/wr/rd/wdata      +------+-------+
                        win_rdata (ID, COUNT)           | count[13:0] (binary)
                                                        v
                                               +-----------------+
                                               | seg_display     |--> SEG[7:0] (registered)
                                               | BCD + 4-digit   |--> AN[7:0]  (registered)
                                               | scan, 1 ms slot |
                                               +-----------------+
```

Blocks (module, file):

| Name | Function |
|---|---|
| top (rtl/top.sv) | board top: resets, instantiates every block below and fpga_shell, ties AN4..AN7 high |
| reset_sync (shell) | synchronises CPU_RESETN into CLK100MHZ, active-high reset (async assert, sync release) |
| btn_debounce (rtl/btn_debounce.sv) | sync2 on BTNC, counts consecutive high cycles, one-cycle clr pulse after DEBOUNCE_CYCLES |
| seg1_counter (rtl/seg1_counter.sv) | 27-bit tick counter (ONE_SEC_CYCLES), 14-bit binary count 0..9999, clear on clr_pulse, window register map (ID at 0x00, COUNT at 0x04 as window offsets 0x80 / 0x84 are the shell's; see register map) |
| seg_display (rtl/seg_display.sv) | binary to four BCD digits (double dabble), digit scan counter (SCAN_CYCLES), segment decode, registered SEG and AN outputs |
| fpga_shell (shell) | UART 115200 8N1 line, frame protocol, register window |

## Register map (through the shell window)

The shell owns 0x00 to 0x7F. The design's registers sit in the window at 0x80 and up.
The spec's offsets are the design's offsets, so the window addresses are the shell address minus 0x80.

| Shell ADDR | Window win_addr | Name | Access | Reset | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x80 | 0x00 | ID | RO | 0x53454731 | ASCII "SEG1" (byte 3 = S) |
| 0x84 | 0x04 | COUNT | RO | 0x00000000 | bits [15:0] binary count, 0..9999; bits 31:16 = 0 |

Read-only: win_wr is ignored. The count is read live (no snapshot), as the spec defaults say.

## Clock plan

| Domain | Port | Frequency | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| clk | CLK100MHZ | 100 MHz (10 ns) | the only clock; tick, debounce, scan and UART all on it; no gated or derived clocks; tick is a clock-enable |

## Reset plan

- CPU_RESETN (active low, async to the board) goes through `reset_sync` (the only asynchronous-assert element,
  a reset synchroniser). Its active-high output `rst` is the only reset inside the design.
